identity.title: The Core Mass Function across Galactic Environments. III. Massive Protoclusters

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we measure the CMF in 28 dense clumps within 3.5 kpc that are likely to be central regions of massive protoclusters, observed via $1.3\:{\rm{mm}}$ dust continuum emission by the ALMAGAL project.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.00195.L.

question.value: What is the shape of the core mass function (CMF) in massive protoclusters within 3.5 kpc, whether it shows a break, and how does it compare to the CMF in other environments like G286 and IRDCs?

evidence.quote: Here we measure the CMF in 28 dense clumps within 3.5 kpc that are likely to be central regions of massive protoclusters, observed via $1.3\:{\rm{mm}}$ dust continuum emission by the ALMAGAL project.
We compare this massive protocluster CMF with those derived using the same methods in the G286 protocluster and a sample of Infrared Dark Clouds.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.00195.L.
observed via $1.3\:{\rm{mm}}$ dust continuum emission by the ALMAGAL project.
ALMAGAL was designed to observe continuum and line emission near $1.4\:$mm
we limited our analysis to sources within 3.5 kpc that had 12m-array observations delivered to the ALMA archive by May 2020.

findings_qualitative.value: Statistically robust detection of a break in the power-law behavior of the true CMF located between ~5 and 15 M_sun.

evidence.quote: However, we find evidence of a break in this power-law behavior between $\sim5$ and $15\:M_{\odot}$, which is, to our knowledge, the first time such a break has been found in distant ($\gtrsim 1$ kpc) regions by ALMA.

findings_qualitative.value: The massive protocluster CMF is significantly more top-heavy, containing more massive cores, than the CMFs of G286 and IRDCs.

evidence.loc: Comparison of CMFs in Different Environments and Implications for Massive Star Formation
evidence.quote: The nature of the difference is that we find that the CMF from our sample of ALMAGAL-observed massive protoclusters has a significantly larger population of high-mass cores than the CMFs derived from the G286 protocluster and the IRDC clumps.

findings_qualitative.value: Clustering analysis shows Q parameters between 0.64 and 0.82, showing little evidence for centrally condensed structures in individual clumps.

evidence.quote: We found little evidence for centrally condensed structures in these regions, with values of $Q$ ranging from 0.64 to 0.82, as summarized in Table 3.

claims.hypothesis: The CMF in distant massive protoclusters follows a single Salpeter-like power law across all core masses >= 1 M_sun
claims.experiment: Fit single power laws (WLS, MLE, MLE-B) across standard range M_min = 0.79 M_sun and evaluate goodness of fit with KS and AD bootstrap resampling and AICc
claims.result: Single power-law fits starting at 0.79 M_sun fail with p < 0.001 and alpha ~ 0.50-0.60; single power law only acceptable above ~5 M_sun with alpha = 0.94 +/- 0.08 (p = 0.12)
claims.finding: The single power law hypothesis across the full range is rejected; a break in power-law behavior exists between ~5 and 15 M_sun

evidence.loc: Single Power-Law Fits to the CMF
evidence.quote: We also note that a single power law fit over this mass range is not a very accurate description of the CMFs, which is indicated by the fits having very low $p$ values ($<0.001$).

We studied where power-law behavior is likely to begin in the CMF through analyzing the behavior of the the corrected Akaike Information Criterion and Anderson-Darling and Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics, and found that a “break” in the power-law behavior of the true CMF is indicated between $\sim$5 to $15 \ M_{\odot}$.

claims.hypothesis: The CMF is universal and independent of clump mass surface density environment
claims.experiment: Perform KS tests comparing the True CMF from ALMAGAL massive protoclusters to those derived with identical methods in G286 and IRDC clumps
claims.result: KS test yields p < 0.001 comparing True CMF to G286 and p < 0.001 comparing to IRDCs, with massive protoclusters having a higher fraction of massive cores
claims.finding: The CMF is not universal across environments; massive protoclusters with Sigma_cl > 1 g cm^-2 produce significantly more top-heavy CMFs than lower Sigma_cl regions

evidence.loc: Comparison of CMFs in Different Environments and Implications for Massive Star Formation
evidence.quote: From this analysis we find significant differences between the populations. The true CMF is significantly different than the true CMFs of Paper I ($p < .001$) and Paper II ($p < .001$).

evidence.loc: Comparison of CMFs in Different Environments and Implications for Massive Star Formation
evidence.quote: Thus, we conclude that this difference in environmental conditions is the factor that is most likely to be responsible for the variation in the observed CMFs.

claims.hypothesis: A single log-normal distribution is a better descriptor of the True CMF than piecewise power laws
claims.experiment: Calculate Vuong log-likelihood ratio test R and Akaike weights AICc comparing log-normal vs power-law / PPL fits
claims.result: For True CMF, Vuong test shows no significant preference for log-normal over power-law (R = -1.2, p = 0.25); AICc weights strongly favor double PPL (w_double = 0.85) over log-normal (w_ln = 0.03)
claims.finding: A single log-normal is not a better fit to the True CMF compared to a double piecewise power law

evidence.quote: However, there was no significant evidence that a log-normal was a better descriptor of the true CMF than a single power-law ($R=-1.2$, $p=.25$).

In summary, these results indicate that a single log-normal is not a better fit of the true CMF compared to a double PPL, at least over the range of masses explored in this study, down to about $1\:M_\odot$.

why_this_data.value: Sources selected within 3.5 kpc that had delivered 12m-array data from the ALMAGAL survey to allow probing down to low core masses (~1 M_sun)

evidence.quote: To be able to probe down to relatively low core masses, i.e., $\sim1\:M_\odot$, we limited our analysis to sources within 3.5 kpc that had 12m-array observations delivered to the ALMA archive by May 2020.

why_this_method.value: Adopted the exact dendrogram extraction and flux/number recovery correction methods of Papers I and II to enable direct, unbiased comparison between environments

evidence.quote: To identify cores, we followed the methods used in our studies of the G286 protocluster (Paper I) and IRDCs (Paper II), thus allowing a direct comparison of the derived CMFs.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using clumpfind algorithm instead of dendrograms was explored in Paper I and rejected in favor of the fiducial dendrogram leaf method

evidence.quote: We note that the effects of using the clumpfind algorithm (cite: williams_determining_1994) instead of the dendrogram method were explored in Paper I, and we do not repeat this analysis here.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Identifying cores on primary-beam-corrected images was rejected because varying noise across pointings would compromise extraction

evidence.quote: Attempting to identify cores in primary-beam-corrected images would be compromised as a result of this effect.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance was supplemented/deprioritized relative to Anderson-Darling distance because KS is insensitive to distribution tails

evidence.loc: Single Power-Law Fits to the CMF
evidence.quote: We prefer the AD statistic due to the known issue of the KS statistic being insensitive to differences in the tails of compared distributions.

limitations_admitted.value: Core masses lack local background subtraction and assume a uniform dust temperature of 20 K without core-scale temperature measurements

evidence.quote: The core masses we report have significant uncertainties due to no correction being made for the local backgrounds within which the cores are embedded, and also from a lack of temperature information on the scales of the cores.

limitations_admitted.value: Small number of cores per clump (Nc < 30) limits clustering analysis and prevents calculating mass segregation ratios on a per-clump basis

evidence.quote: However, we note that the relatively small sample sizes of cores within each clump severely limit the conclusions that can be derived from these results.

Additionally, the small number of cores in each clump prevented the calculation of the frequently used “mass segregation ratio” $\Lambda_{MSR}$ and other typical methods to investigate this effect on a clump-by-clump basis.

limitations_admitted.value: The sample of 28 clumps is an early subset and not a complete volume-limited sample of massive clumps within 3.5 kpc

evidence.quote: We note that this is not a complete sample of all such massive clumps within 3.5 kpc of the Sun and is only a small fraction of the data that will eventually come from the ALMAGAL survey.

referee_caveats_inferred: Potential bias if warmer dust temperatures systematically exist in more massive cores, which would artificially flatten the high-mass CMF
Uncertainties on number recovery corrections at the low-mass end (< 1 M_sun), especially in more distant (> 3 kpc) clumps, could artificially inflate the lowest-mass bins
Absence of line data to confirm that all dendrogram leaves are gravitationally bound cores rather than transient turbulent density fluctuations

missing_for_reproduction: Exact pipeline-generated continuum FITS image filenames or download dates for the 28 clumps
Detailed numerical tables or functional fits for the f_flux and f_num completeness correction curves as a function of normalized flux
Random seeds or exact coordinates of the 50 beam-sized noise measurement areas per clump
reproducibility.score_reason: The paper provides a very detailed statistical and mathematical methodology, complete tables of clump and core properties (222 cores with coordinates, fluxes, raw/corrected masses, radii, and surface densities), and uses standard open-source Python packages (astrodendro, powerlaw, networkx). However, reproduction requires either adopting the completeness correction curves by digitizing Figure 2 or obtaining the core insertion scripts from Papers I and II, and exact ALMA archive image product versions are not specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All 222 core measurements are fully listed in Table 4, and the statistical fitting pipeline (MLE, MLE-B, KS/AD distance minimization, AICc model comparison) can be directly executed on these tabulated numbers to reproduce the key finding: a break in the CMF between 5 and 15 M_sun and a high-mass power-law slope of alpha ~ 0.94.
